glossary.Parasites: Organisms that live in or on a host and harm it, such as amoebae.
glossary.Ulcerative colitis: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease affecting the rectum and colon.
glossary.Penicillins: A family of beta-lactam antibiotics including amoxicillin.
glossary.Ciprofloxacin: A fluoroquinolone antibiotic strongly linked to C. difficile.
glossary.Dehydration: Loss of body water faster than it is replaced.
glossary.Abdominal cramps: Spasms of colicky pain in the abdomen.
glossary.Self-limiting: Gets better on its own without treatment.
glossary.Antigen: A molecule that the immune system or a test recognises; for C. diff, the GDH enzyme.
glossary.Toxin: A poison made by a bacterium; C. diff toxins A and B cause disease.
glossary.Creatinine: A muscle waste product cleared by the kidneys; a rise shows kidney injury.
glossary.Septic parameters: Signs of sepsis such as fever, tachycardia, hypotension or raised lactate.
glossary.Dilatation: Widening of a hollow organ such as the colon.
glossary.Opioids: Strong painkillers like morphine that slow gut motility.
glossary.Stool culture: Growing organisms from a stool sample to identify the cause.
glossary.Toxin testing: A stool test detecting C. difficile toxins, proving active infection.
glossary.PCR: Polymerase chain reaction: a test that detects an organism's DNA.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.CRP: C-reactive protein, a blood marker of inflammation.
glossary.U&Es: Urea and electrolytes, a blood test of kidney function and salts.
glossary.CT abdomen: A cross-sectional X-ray scan of the abdomen.
glossary.Antibiotic-associated colitis: Colitis triggered by antibiotics, usually from C. difficile.
glossary.Recurrent episode: Return of infection after it had resolved.
glossary.Infection prevention: Measures to stop infection spreading between patients.
glossary.0.9% saline: Normal saline, a salt solution used for IV fluid replacement.
glossary.Colonic mucosal cells: The cells lining the inside of the colon.
glossary.Proctoscopy: Looking inside the rectum and anus through a short tube.
glossary.Germinate: When a dormant spore turns back into an active, multiplying bacterium.
glossary.Motility: The gut's ability to move contents along by muscular contraction.
glossary.Perforation: A hole through the wall of the bowel.
glossary.Sepsis: Life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated response to infection.
glossary.Alcohol gel: Hand rub that kills most bacteria and viruses but not C. difficile spores.
